name: Higher-Order Thinking
description: Bloom's taxonomy cognitive domain: scaffolded progression through six levels — Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create — from lower-order recall to higher-order synthesis

steps.name: Remember - Recall facts and basic concepts
steps.description:
Recognize or recall relevant facts, terms, basic concepts, and answers from the knowledge graph and prior context

Bloom's taxonomy Level 1 (lower-order): retrieve knowledge from long-term memory. Identify the key terminology, facts, dates, definitions, and established concepts relevant to the problem at hand. Catalog what is already known before attempting to interpret or apply it.

SearchMemories.reason: Retrieve established facts, definitions, and prior knowledge from the knowledge graph — the cognitive recall operation

BuildContext.reason: Identify relevant concepts and their relationships as stored knowledge

stop_conditions: Key facts, terms, and definitions recalled and cataloged
Prior knowledge relevant to the problem retrieved from memory
Factual foundation established before interpretation begins
next_actions: Proceed to Understand — organize and interpret recalled information

steps.name: Understand - Organize and explain meaning
steps.description:
Demonstrate understanding of recalled facts and ideas by organizing, summarizing, and explaining their meaning

Bloom's taxonomy Level 2 (lower-order): construct meaning from recalled information. Classify, describe, discuss, explain, and summarize the facts gathered in the Remember step. Translate raw facts into coherent explanations. Identify the relationships between concepts and express them in your own formulation.

BuildContext.reason: Map relationships between recalled concepts to construct coherent understanding

stop_conditions: Recalled facts organized into coherent categories or themes
Key relationships between concepts explained in own formulation
Information summarized — demonstrating comprehension beyond rote recall
next_actions: Proceed to Apply — use understood knowledge in context

steps.name: Apply - Use knowledge in new situations
steps.description:
Use acquired and understood knowledge to solve problems in new or unfamiliar situations

Bloom's taxonomy Level 3 (lower-order): carry out or use a procedure in a given situation. Execute known methods, implement established procedures, or transfer understood concepts to novel contexts. This is the bridge between comprehension and the higher-order cognitive operations.

SearchMemories.reason: Find analogous solved problems, established procedures, and applicable frameworks in the knowledge graph

stop_conditions: Understood knowledge applied to the specific problem at hand
Known methods or procedures executed in the new context
Transfer of learning from familiar to novel situation demonstrated
next_actions: Proceed to Analyze — break down and examine component relationships

steps.name: Analyze - Break down and examine relationships
steps.description:
Break down information into constituent parts and determine how parts relate to one another and to an overall structure or purpose

🧠 SEQUENTIAL THINKING REQUIRED: Use the SequentialThinking tool to work through this systematically.

Bloom's taxonomy Level 4 (higher-order): differentiate, organize, and attribute. Decompose the problem into component elements. Identify the relationships, motives, and causes between parts. Distinguish relevant from irrelevant information. Determine how elements fit together into a structure.

SequentialThinking.reason: Systematic decomposition into parts and relationship mapping requires structured analytical reasoning — the first higher-order cognitive level in Bloom's revised taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl, 2001)

BuildContext.reason: Explore structural relationships and hidden connections between components

stop_conditions: Information decomposed into constituent parts
Relationships, motives, and causes between parts identified
Relevant distinguished from irrelevant elements
Overall structure or organizing principle articulated
next_actions: Proceed to Evaluate — judge quality and make criterion-based assessments

steps.name: Evaluate - Make criterion-based judgments
steps.description:
Make judgments about the value of ideas, materials, or methods based on criteria and standards

🧠 SEQUENTIAL THINKING REQUIRED: Use the SequentialThinking tool to work through this systematically.

Bloom's taxonomy Level 5 (higher-order): check and critique. Assess the quality, credibility, and significance of analytical findings against explicit criteria. Judge whether conclusions are supported by evidence. Detect inconsistencies, fallacies, and gaps. Appraise which elements are most important and why.

SequentialThinking.reason: Criterion-based judgment requires weighing evidence against standards, checking internal consistency, and detecting fallacies — complex evaluative cognition per Bloom's revised taxonomy

SearchMemories.reason: Retrieve evaluation criteria, quality standards, and comparable assessments from knowledge graph

stop_conditions: Explicit evaluation criteria established and applied
Quality and credibility of analytical findings judged
Inconsistencies, fallacies, and gaps detected
Evaluative conclusions supported by evidence and reasoning
next_actions: Proceed to Create — synthesize a new whole from evaluated elements

steps.name: Create - Synthesize new understanding
steps.description:
Combine elements to form a coherent, functional, or novel whole — reorganize into a new pattern or structure

🧠 SEQUENTIAL THINKING REQUIRED: Use the SequentialThinking tool to work through this systematically.

Bloom's taxonomy Level 6 (higher-order): generate, plan, and produce. Synthesize the analyzed and evaluated elements into an original product, plan, or proposal. Combine ideas to create new meaning that did not exist before. This is the highest cognitive level — producing something that is more than the sum of its parts.

SequentialThinking.reason: Generative synthesis requires combining evaluated elements into novel structures — the highest cognitive operation in Bloom's revised taxonomy, demanding creative integration

WriteMemory.reason: Persist the novel synthesis as institutional memory with full derivation chain

stop_conditions: New coherent whole synthesized from analyzed and evaluated elements
Product, plan, or proposal represents genuine creative integration
Synthesis grounded in the prior five cognitive levels
Novel insight or structure documented that transcends individual components
next_actions: Document synthesized output with full cognitive derivation chain
